acceptanceCriteria.description: The development command establishes only missing approved prerequisites before Forge, rechecks them, passes the selected interpreter to Desktop, and exits safely with a useful reason when setup cannot complete. A second run reuses a verified installation.

Desktop opens its shell only after the host verifies required Python installation. Missing, unsupported, incomplete and failed checks keep the shell inert and show a fixed, actionable message. Optional software stays outside this required check.

An isolated Windows x64 development checkout with no compatible Python establishes the approved prerequisites and opens Desktop. A repeat launch reuses them. A packaged Desktop startup with a deliberately unavailable required runtime keeps the loading screen in its failure state. Exercise equivalent cases for each additional approved platform before claiming support for it.

Verify exact supplier and digest before execution. Prove refusal of unapproved artifacts and platforms, interruption and concurrent setup behavior, non-elevated checkout ownership, preservation of existing user data, and redacted failure outputs.
